bib.title: Fact, Fetch, and Reason: A Unified Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation

question: How well do LLMs perform end-to-end RAG that needs factual recall, multi-document retrieval and reasoning together, rather than each in isolation?
hypothesis: Forcing a model to retrieve and reason over several steps should improve accuracy over single-step inference.
contributions: FRAMES, a dataset of 824 test samples to evaluate retrieval and reasoning across multiple documents in a unified framework
Evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs on factuality, retrieval and reasoning
Empirical insights on limits of LLMs in multi-hop and temporal reasoning
A multi-step retrieval and reasoning framework raising accuracy from 0.408 (single-step) to 0.66

method.summary: Human annotators wrote 824 multi-hop questions over 2-15 Wikipedia articles, labelled with five reasoning types. Models are evaluated with a naive prompt, BM25-retrieved context, an oracle prompt with gold articles, and an iterative LLM-generated-query BM25 pipeline; correctness is judged by an LLM autorater.
method.task: multi-hop open-domain QA / end-to-end RAG evaluation over Wikipedia

datasets.name: FRAMES
datasets.source: Human-written questions over Wikipedia articles; released at huggingface.co/datasets/google/frames-benchmark
datasets.preprocessing: Re-annotated three months later, filtering 5.5% of samples whose answer was no longer true; temporal disambiguation added (e.g. 'As of August 1, 2024'); yes/no questions removed

datasets.name: Wikipedia dump (BM25 index)
datasets.source: Wikipedia data dump (tinyurl link in footnote 2)
datasets.preprocessing: BM25 score computed between query and every article; whole articles are returned

inference.prompting: Single-step: naive prompt; BM25-R (n_docs=2 or 4); Oracle (all gold articles). Multi-step: Algorithm 1 over n iterations, k queries per iteration, top n_docs BM25 articles each, only new documents added; vanilla vs with search-planning instructions (few examples of ideal query sequence, do not repeat queries, think step-by-step). Prompt texts for planning not printed.
inference.retrieval: BM25 over a Wikipedia dump, top n_docs articles per query; best setting (k, n, n_docs) = (5, 5, 10)

other.cost: five non-parallelizable retrieval calls plus one final answering call per question for n=5

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction of questions where an LLM autorater (Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514, prompt in Fig 6) judges the gold answer present in the model response

metrics.name: Recall of gold articles in context
metrics.definition: Share of gold Wikipedia articles present in context after BM25 retrieval

eval.protocol: LLM autorater validated against human evaluation (accuracy 0.96, Cohen's Kappa 0.889). No seeds, repeated runs, or significance tests reported.

prompts.text: System: You are a helpful assistant. User: """TASK: You will be provided with {k_context} Wikipedia article extracts. Based on these extracts, generate {n_questions} challenging factoid questions that meet the following criteria: 1. Standalone & Context-Independent ... 2. Unambiguous Answer ... 3. Multi-hop Reasoning: Answering each question should require combining information from ALL {k_context} provided Wikipedia articles. 4. Grounded in Context & Conceptual Format ... {WIKI ARTICLES}""" (abridged; full text in Fig 5)

===Task=== I need your help in evaluating an answer provided by an LLM against a ground truth answer. Your task is to determine if the ground truth answer is present in the LLM's response. ... Provide your final evaluation in the following format: "Explanation:" (How you made the decision?) "Decision:" ("TRUE" or "FALSE" )
Create n factoid questions that demand multi-hop reasoning based on information found across multiple Wikipedia articles. (abridged; full in Fig 7)

limits: Authors concede possible pretraining contamination from Wikipedia, which may inflate scores.
Authors concede the dataset may not represent the full range of real-world queries.
Multi-step retrieval is expensive: six non-parallelizable calls per question at n=5; authors hope future work reduces search calls.
Only BM25 over Wikipedia is used; no dense retriever tested. The paper says it fixes retrieval to isolate search planning.
Best multi-step result (0.66) is shown only in Fig 4, with no table, variance, seeds or repeated runs; decoding settings, temperature and planning prompts are not given.
Small models (Gemma, Llama, Qwen) were not run with longer-context settings due to context limits.
Autorater is the same model family as the main evaluated model (Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514), with unstated validation sample size.
Models are May-October 2024 vintage and have dated.

code.snippet: Initialize context C <- {Q}; for iteration i = 1 to n: for query j = 1 to k: generate search query Qij based on context C; retrieve top n_docs documents Dij using BM25 based on Qij; C <- C ∪ (Dij \ C); end; end; generate final response R using context C
